scope: Pinned Frida 17.24.3 Gum CModule source capability review; no native execution or production changes.

report.conclusion: No complete direct CModule-supported sequence exists for the required native listener/interceptor/cloak operations in the pinned source. Of the ten names, only g_object_unref is in the curated CModule headers and generated builtin table. CModule bypasses image discovery for supported builtins, but cannot supply these other nine merely by declaring their prototypes.

source_anchors.fact: Documented curated subset; optional symbols argument supplies caller-provided pointers. CModule.builtins provides defines and headers, not arbitrary native operation addresses.
Curated interceptor header contains invocation context accessors and gum_interceptor_get_current_invocation; no attach/options/listener factory/ignore APIs.
Generator reads curated runtime headers, architecture writer header and Capstone headers; it does not import every public Gum header.
Builtin symbols are derived from declarations in selected headers and inserted as direct compiled function addresses.
TinyCC unresolved symbols resolve against generated builtin table; no fallback to native global export discovery.
Darwin external-toolchain mapper resolves caller-provided symbols then same builtin table; choosing external does not add missing Gum APIs.
CModule.builtins getter returns only defines and headers.
Full native header supports UNIGNORABLE attach option, absent from curated CModule header.
JS attach accepts native callback pointers but initializes GumAttachOptions to zero and only fills instrumentation and listener_function_data; CModule callback alone remains ignorable.
V8 attach likewise initializes native attach options to zero; no ignorability assignment present in binding source.
Supported JS Cloak methods call this binding instance Gum cloak functions directly, but do not expose native function pointers or descriptor ownership provenance.

rejected_assumptions: A public native GUM_API declaration implies inclusion in CModule builtins or export visibility inside packaged frida-agent.
Copying full Gum prototypes or selecting external toolchain adds absent builtin symbols.
Supplying a CModule callback to JS Interceptor.attach makes it unignorable.
CModule.builtins exposes a hidden supported symbol-address dictionary.
A separately linked Gum library establishes the same agent instance or preserves existing descriptor registry ownership.
The prior inconclusive exported-symbol lookup proves native APIs absent.

smallest_discriminating_probe.status: unrun; no dispatch authorized by this bounded source task
smallest_discriminating_probe.purpose: Optional actual-wheel confirmation of curated builtins: per-symbol compile/link without invoking the operations, with embedded invocation helper and g_object_unref positive controls. No image discovery, hooks, descriptor manipulation or compiler workloads.
smallest_discriminating_probe.expected_from_source: Two controls link; remaining nine names fail to link. A contrary actual result requires reconciling packaged runtime with pinned source before native calls.
smallest_discriminating_probe.limits: Does not satisfy ignored/unignorable differential, descriptor ownership or safe uncloak-before-reuse gate. Since source exposes no complete supported sequence, this is not claimed as a production unblocker.

report.remaining_gate: No identified supported direct-CModule path to same-agent unignorable attach and native descriptor lifecycle hooks. Parent must decide next supported boundary; this report does not choose replacement strategy or weaken whole-job cleanup.
